title: Viant Provides Clearer View of Purchase Behavior for Advertisers through Expanded Commerce Data Partnerships
summary: Viant expands commerce data partnerships to help CPG and retail advertisers activate purchase-based audiences and measure incremental sales.

# Viant Provides Clearer View of Purchase Behavior for Advertisers through Expanded Commerce Data Partnerships


November 17, 2026 in[Blog](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/)


***By Keith Petri, SVP, Data & Identity* , Viant**


## Key Takeaways


- Viant is bringing purchase, transaction and point-of-sale signals from ABCS Insights, Affinity Solutions, Attain, Fetch, and Becausal together in the Viant Advertising Platform.
- By resolving these strategic signals to Viant’s[household-level identity graph,](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/planning-and-buying/household-id/) advertisers can build a more complete view of purchase behavior across retailers, brands, categories and products.
- CPG and retail marketers can activate audiences based on actual purchase behavior, not just browsing or inferred interest.
- Fresh commerce data can inform campaigns before and during the flight, while Viant’s Advanced Reporting suite connects media exposure to incremental sales post campaign.
- Advertisers can measure outcomes at the retailer, brand, and item level, including market share and SKU-level sales lift, where applicable.


---


For CPG and retail marketers, the most important media question often comes after the impression is served: did the advertising move your product?


That is the question Viant aims to answer by expanding its commerce data partnerships with ABCS Insights, Affinity Solutions, Attain, Fetch, and Becausal. By bringing verified purchase, transaction and point-of-sale signals onto the Viant advertising platform, these partnerships give marketers a clearer view of shopping behavior across retailers, brands, categories, and products. Advertisers can use that intelligence to build audiences based on actual purchases, activate campaigns across channels, and measure whether media is driving incremental sales.


The need for that connected view becomes clear when you look at how people actually shop. Someone might buy Goldfish snacks at the supermarket one week, pick up a multi-pack at a warehouse club the next, and grab a single-serving bag at a convenience store on the way to work. Each retailer sees only its own slice of that shopper’s purchases, and no single source sees the full picture. That makes it harder for the marketers of Goldfish to understand who is buying their products, where those purchases happen, and whether their advertising is driving sales.


Until now, brands and agencies have had to stitch these signals together from separate data sources. Viant is bringing those fragmented signals together on a single platform, giving advertisers a more complete and connected view of commerce behavior and a clearer way to connect media exposure with sales.


## The Gap Between “Seen” and “Sold”


Impression data is abundant, but connecting that exposure to real-world purchases is the more challenging problem of digital advertising. Purchase data is scattered across retailers, consumer data ecosystems and providers, each holding a different fragment of the full picture. A retailer sees everything in its own stores, but nothing beyond them.


A consumer data ecosystem consists of shoppers who opt in to share their purchase data, providing visibility into shopping behaviors across retailers and a representative sample of households. A card feed sees the transaction, but not always the item or individual SKU.


For CPG and retail marketers, the result has historically been an incomplete view of whether media exposure translated into business growth.


## From Scattered Signals to a Single Household View


Viant aims to solve this fragmentation by connecting:


- **Receipt-level and transaction data** , which captures what consumers buy down to the individual item, category and brand.
- **Merchant-level card and bank data** , which extends visibility across retailers of every size, including hard-to-measure channels like specialty and club retail.
- **Point-of-sale signals** , which add a view of what’s happening at the register.


The key is that each signal is resolved to Viant’s proprietary household-level identity graph, anchored in physical address, rather than identifiers controlled by big tech. This gives advertisers a unified view of SKU, category, brand and retailer purchase behavior instead of four disconnected datasets. Together, they show far more than any one source could on its own.


A[household view](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/planning-and-buying/household-id/) is especially important because media exposure and purchase behavior do not always come from the same individual. One household member may see an ad on a connected TV while another completes the purchase in-store or online. By connecting those actions at the household level, Viant can tie the impression to the resulting purchase without treating the viewer and buyer as unrelated consumers.


This matters especially for CTV. Premium CTV is where households spend their attention, but proving what that does for sales has been a persistent challenge. By tying exposure to SKU and transaction-level purchase outcomes at the household level, Viant helps close that gap.


## What Each Partner Brings to the Cart


- **ABCS Insights** works with Viant to enable advertisers to build audiences from verified purchase behavior and measure sales impact with one consistent approach across all verticals, screens, retailers, and channels. That full-funnel, cross-media measurement uses experimental design methodology to tie media exposure to purchases within the same household. Behind it all is purchase data covering approximately 40 million U.S. households across more than 15,000 retailers and correlating 99.7% with reported U.S. retailer sales.
- **Affinity Solutions** provides permissioned debit- and credit-card transaction data covering 195 million consumers. The data is refreshed through daily transaction feeds and enriched with geolocation, demographic, and behavioral data. Affinity Solutions packages these purchase signals into solutions for consumer insights, audience development and purchase-lift measurement.
- **Attain** operates a comprehensive, permissioned consumer data ecosystem built through its owned-and-operated financial service applications, where more than 14 million U.S. consumers opt in to share their purchase activity. Because permissioned consumers share their checking, debit, credit, loyalty accounts, receipts, and email, Attain sees item-level purchases across retailers, online and in-store, with data refreshed daily. Their consumer ecosystem is census-balanced to the U.S. population and uses advanced modeling to scale that foundation to national-scale reach. Attain supports audience development, activation, optimization and measurement across retailers and channels.
- **Fetch** delivers a comprehensive view of what consumers actually buy, capturing more than 100 million receipts a week representing a quarter-trillion dollars in annual consumer spending. Fetch Data transforms its extensive retail-agnostic, SKU-level view of household spending into actionable intelligence across the advertising ecosystem, powering smarter targeting, more precise measurement and better business outcomes by bringing real-world purchase intelligence into every media decision.
- **Becausal** , formerly Scanbuy’s data division, provides multi-source CPG purchase data and audience solutions covering more than 30 million monthly active shoppers. Its offering includes cross-retailer and cross-brand purchase taxonomies, purchase-based audiences, causal-AI-powered audience extension and auditable audience decisioning. Becausal’s data supports targeting, activation, measurement and sales-lift use cases.


Individually, each of these expanded partnerships offers a clearer view of one part of the shopper’s journey. Together, they build on Viant’s existing commerce data partnerships and household-level identity graph to create a more expansive view of purchase behavior— something much closer to the whole basket.


“Commerce intelligence is only as strong as the scale and granularity of its underlying data. Affinity Solutions brings deterministic, verified debit and credit card transaction data representing 195 million consumers to provide a direct view of actual spending across retailers and channels rather than relying on inconsistent proxy metrics,” said Kaylan Lanka, Chief Product Officer of Affinity Solutions. “Combined with Viant’s household-level identity and activation capabilities, these signals enable advertisers to reach high-value audiences, measure incremental sales, and gain a clearer view of real-world outcomes.”


## Turn Purchase Signals Into Campaign Intelligence


The real value of these signals shows up across the entire campaign lifecycle.


- **Before launch** , advertisers can build audiences from actual purchase behavior, using syndicated or custom segments they can activate directly in the Viant DSP. That means finding likely buyers based on what households have bought, not just what they’ve browsed.
- **During the flight** , direct pipes into the platform, including ingestion through[Viant’s Conversion API](https://docs.api.viantinc.com/reference/how-to-get-started) , keep purchase data fresh enough to inform decisions while a campaign is still running, not weeks after it ends.
- **After the campaign** , the same data flows into Viant’s[Advanced Reporting](https://www.viantinc.com/solutions/advanced-reporting/) suite to power closed-loop sales measurement: incremental Sales Lift, exposure-based attribution, and retailer- and item-level sales breakdowns. Advertisers can see not just whether sales moved, but where, at which retailers and for which products, including market-share reporting.


## A More Complete Picture of the Shopper


These integrations are live within the Viant ad platform today, and we’ll continue to add data onboarding and reporting capabilities over the coming quarters.


If you’re a CPG or retail marketer who wants to see how purchase-based audiences and closed-loop measurement could work for your brand, we’d love to talk. Reach out to your Viant representative, or learn more at[viantinc.com](https://viantinc.com/) .

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is a cookieless DSP?Expand


A cookieless DSP is a programmatic advertising platform that identifies and reaches audiences using durable, privacy-first identifiers rather than third-party cookies.


Instead of relying on fragile browser tracking, these platforms leverage advanced solutions like Household ID™ to maintain scale and precision. This approach ensures that digital campaigns remain effective and measurable regardless of evolving browser restrictions or privacy regulations.


How does programmatic advertising work without cookies?Expand


Programmatic advertising functions without cookies by activating first-party data through identity resolution frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 and the Household ID. Marketers also utilize contextual targeting to align ads with real-time content and prioritize natively cookieless channels such as CTV and DOOH. These methods allow for high-impact reach and frequency management without the need for invasive user-level tracking.


What is the difference between a DSP and a cookieless DSP?Expand


Traditional DSPs rely on syncing third-party cookies across exchanges to build audience profiles, a process that is increasingly fragmented and unreliable. A cookieless DSP uses people-based identity, first-party data, and privacy-safe signals to reach consumers across all devices.


Viant DSP was purpose-built to be cookieless from the ground up, ensuring it never relied on the legacy infrastructure of third-party cookies.


What targeting options are available in a cookieless environment?Expand


Marketers in a cookieless environment can utilize a robust suite of options including contextual targeting, first-party data onboarding, and household-level identity resolution.


Furthermore, interoperability with alternative ID frameworks like Unified ID 2.0 allows brands to maintain significant scale across the open web. These diverse tactics provide a durable, privacy-forward alternative to outdated cookie-based audience segments.


How is campaign performance measured in a cookieless world?Expand


In a cookieless world, campaign measurement is achieved through modern attribution models such as[incrementality testing](https://www.viantinc.com/insights/blog/incrementality-and-incrementality-testing-a-primer/) , Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), and secure data clean rooms.


The Household ID serves as a critical cross-device attribution layer, linking high-impact exposures on CTV to conversions on other digital devices within the home. This transition allows advertisers to prove ROI and optimize spend without relying on fragmented, cookie-based signals.
